evals.name: Over-engineered God Class Audit & Simplification
evals.prompt: Review this 350-line OrderManager class that handles database transactions, PDF generation, email sending, discount calculations, and credit card charging. Identify violations of Single Responsibility, High Cohesion, and KISS, and propose a decoupled, maintainable architecture.
evals.expected_output: A structured Programming Fundamentals Audit identifying concrete violations (SRP, High Cohesion, KISS, SoC) and a step-by-step refactoring plan following 'Do the Simplest Thing That Could Possibly Work'.
assertions: Identifies violation of Single Responsibility Principle with distinct reasons to change
Identifies violation of Separation of Concerns between IO/persistence and business calculation
Applies 'Do the Simplest Thing That Could Possibly Work' rather than introducing unnecessary microservices or abstract factories
Adheres to the structured Audit Output Template

evals.name: Demeter & Exception Swallowing PR Review
evals.prompt: Review this PR diff: user.getCompany().getBillingPlan().getDiscountTier().apply() and an empty except block that ignores all database exceptions. Provide a code review grounded in fundamental principles.
evals.expected_output: Review citing Law of Demeter / Information Hiding for the object train wreck, and Principle of Least Astonishment / Write Code for the Maintainer for the silent exception suppression.
assertions: Explicitly references Law of Demeter (Least Knowledge) and suggests delegation
Flags the swallowed exception under Principle of Least Astonishment and Write Code for the Maintainer
Provides clear, runnable before/after code refactoring snippets

evals.name: DRY vs YAGNI Dilemma Arbitration
evals.prompt: Our team has two similar functions in two different microservices calculating customer tax. One engineer wants to create a new shared NPM package with generic plugin interfaces. The other wants to leave them as-is. Arbitrate this decision using programming fundamentals.
evals.expected_output: Balanced arbitration citing Sandi Metz's rule ('Duplication is cheaper than the wrong abstraction'), YAGNI, Low Coupling, and the Rule of Three / AHA.
assertions: References DRY, YAGNI, and Low Coupling across microservice boundaries
Applies the Rule of Three / AHA heuristic before creating a shared dependency
Considers the cost of cross-service coupling vs identical code duplication

evals.name: Refactoring Class Hierarchy to Functional Composition & Immutability
evals.prompt: We have a 4-level class inheritance tree (ReportGenerator -> CsvReport -> FormattedCsvReport -> FilteredReport) that mutates an internal state buffer in-place during generation. Refactor this to use functional programming reusability: pure functions, higher-order functions, and function composition.
evals.expected_output: A refactored pipeline using small, stateless pure functions composed together, parameterizing filters and formatters as higher-order function arguments with immutable data transformations.
assertions: Replaces deep inheritance hierarchy with functional composition
Demonstrates pure functions with zero in-place mutations
Uses Higher-Order Functions (HOFs) to parameterize formatting and filtering
Explains the reusability and predictability gains over class mixins
